item.title: Healing Arts One-Time Workshop — Mon Oct 26, 10:00 AM — Pence Gallery
item.description:
Healing Arts One-Time Workshop in Davis Monday, October 26, 10-11:45 AM $5 Members, $10 Non-Members (all materials included)
Part of the Pence’s Healing Arts Program and run by facilitator Amy Vidra, this one-time workshop focuses more broadly on themes related to depression, anxiety, or major life changes. Through the process of art making, participants will have opportunities for discussion, education, and connecting with peers in a safe and supportive space.
Registration is required in advance through our website, and space is limited to the first 8 participants who register. Participants must be 18 or older, and no art experience is necessary. This program is generously sponsored by Bob & Joanne Andresen.
Register here (REQUIRED): https://pencegallery.org/education/programs/workshops-and-classes/
If you register for this session and are unable to attend, please let us know in advance.
Any questions? Email pencegallery@gmail.com.
Source: Visit Davis

item.title: Renegade Orchestra at Davis Odd Fellows — Mon Oct 26, 7:00 PM — Davis Odd Fellows Hall
item.description: Renegade Orchestra in Davis – The Beauty of a Symphony, the Soul of a Rock Band The Renegade Orchestra is the bay area’s most rock and roll symphony. Is it a rock band? Is it an orchestra? Who knows? But it’s definitely the best of both worlds. The pure unbridled fury of some of the bay area’s top orchestra players unleashed on classic rock songs backed up by a hard-hitting rhythm section. The Renegade Orchestra will be performing at Davis Odd Fellows, which is located right in downtown, and is a comfortable and casual hall with great views of the stage. The Renegade Orchestra will rock out to classic songs from Hendrix to Metallica and from Bowie to Zeppelin. At this show, the Renegade Orchestra will present a comfortable, but lively show featuring around top bay area string players combined with a driving rhythm section, all committed to having a relaxed and rocking time. item.title: Portraits of Things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill — Tue Oct 27, 11:30 AM — Pence Gallery
item.description:
Portraits of Things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill at Pence Gallery in Davis Exhibit: October 9 – November 29, 2026 Reception: Friday, October 9, 6-9 PM (Free) Artist Talk: Sunday, November 8, 2-3:30 PM (Free)
Interdisciplinary artist Gioia Fonda has long collected colorful toys, both for their intrinsic charm and as creative inspiration. As a student at California College of the Arts, she arranged small collectibles into still-life compositions, captured them on film, and processed the photos at a local drugstore. Captivated by these arrangements, her advisor, Charlie Gill, painted spare compositions based on her photographs—works that now hang alongside hers. For this exhibition, Fonda has created a series of new paintings featuring similar arrangements of toys and found objects. She is also offering an opportunity for members of the public to exhibit their own small works on paper, riffing on some of her recent photos. Artists may add to this display throughout th

item.title: Bohème Bewitched — Wed Oct 28, 3:00 PM — Bohème Bewitched
item.description:
An enchanted interactive experience from Bohème in Davis, the thrift boutique two blocks away. Quests through a glowing grove, a blacklight zombie forest, a frog bog, a mermaid lagoon, a witch’s cottage and a wood full of wisps. Spooky, not scary. Six enchanted lands inside the old bank at 300 E Street, downtown Davis: the old Union Bank building at the corner of 3rd and E, next to Panera Bread, one block from Central Park. Hours: Wednesday to Friday 3:00 to 6:30pm. Saturday and Sunday 11:00am to 6:30pm. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays. Open 11am to 6:30pm on Saturday, October 31. $4 at the door for the experience, credited to any $8 purchase in the shop (same visit only). Open to all ages every day until 6:30pm. Enchanted Evenings: special evening events run 7 to 9:30pm on Oct 23, 24 and 30. $13 online, $15 at the door. Every date, hours and tickets: bohemebewitched.com
Source: Visit Yolo

item.title: Figure Drawing Group — Wed Oct 28, 6:30 PM — Pence Gallery
item.description:
Figure Drawing Group in Davis Wednesday, October 28, 6:30-9 PM $15 Members, $22 Non-Members | Limited to 10 participants Registration & payment is required in advance through the Pence’s website.
We hold self-guided figure drawing sessions with a nude model every 2nd & 4th Wednesday of the month, from 6:30–9 PM. This group is for both experienced artists and amateurs to have an opportunity to draw from the nude model. If you have never drawn from a live model before and would like to join us, you are very welcome! People of all skill levels, ages 18 and up, are welcome and encouraged to join.
This is not a class, and no instruction is provided. The atmosphere is relaxed and non-competitive. Bring your own art materials, and we’ll provide a comfortable place to sketch or paint live models in our upstairs classroom space. item.title: Tim McNary Live @ The Melon Ball — Thu Oct 29, 7:30 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description:
Tim McNary Live @ The Melon Ball in Davis Tim McNary is a Cinematic Folk Artist from the Southern United States. He found his passion for songwriting while backpacking throughout South America after college. The Nashville based songwriter traverses emotional and geographical borders with multi-dimensional songwriting and evocative vocals. Some of his musical influences include Ben Howard, Foy Vance, & Leif Vollebekk. He’s had dozens of film & tv placements, collaborated with a host of recognized songwriters, and toured extensively around the United States & Canada. Listen to Tim on Spotify or Soundcloud Live Performance Snippets (YouTube) Back to the Beginning (Live – YouTube) Tim’s Website and Instagram $20 General Admission $15 Students (in-store or at the door only, w/ID) $15 Kids under 12 (in-store or at the door only) Doors open at 7:00pm This is a BYOB event!
Source: Visit Davis, Visit Yolo

item.title: Mariachi Bonitas Live at The HIVE — Fri Oct 30, 5:30 PM — The HIVE / Z Specialty Food
item.description:
Live at The HIVE presents Mariachi Bonitas during an outdoor concert. Doors at 5:30pm; Music at 6:30pm. Changing the narrative of mariachi in Sacramento and beyond, Mariachi Bonitas de Dinorah Klingler is redefining what it means to be mariachi. Enjoy a seasonal menu, craft beverages and complimentary honey tasting at northern California’s largest honey and mead tasting room. Pay what you can cover charge: $0-$20/person. Family and dog friendly. All ages welcome. No outside food or drinks.
Source: Visit Yolo

item.title: SSRI R&B Jazz Quintet Live @ The Melon Ball — Fri Oct 30, 7:30 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description:
Live Music @ The Melon Ball in Davis SSRI is a modern jazz collective that is deeply influenced by artists and groups such as: Robert Glasper, Roy Hargrove, and Lettuce. They perform a diverse repertoire of original contemporary jazz arrangements, standards from The American Song Book, and covers of beloved R&B songs from the 90s and mid 2000s. Each band member has a different musical background, but we’ve drawn together due to our shared love of Jazz, R&B, Gospel and Pop music. Join us as we celebrate the music of Michael Jackson, Luther Vandross, Stevie Wonder, and more! $20 General Admission $15 Seniors/Students $10 Kids under 12 Doors open at 7:00pm Cash or Venmo at the door only (no Credit Card) This is a BYOB event!
Source: Visit Davis, Visit Yolo

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Sat Oct 31, 8:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients.
Source: Visit Davis, Visit Yolo

item.title: City of Davis Wetlands Tour — Sun Nov 1, 9:00 AM — 45400 County Road 28H
item.description:
The Davis Wetlands is a managed, native California wetland ecosystem that includes oak riparian woodlands and native grasslands. The group will caravan along the hard-packed gravel roads of the auto tour route. Several stops will be made along the way providing guests with a closer look at the many species of birds that utilize the more than 400 acres of reconstructed wetlands. Meet at the City of Davis Wastewater Treatment Plant. 45400 County Rd 28H, Davis, CA 95616. There is no access to restrooms in the City of Davis Wetlands; please arrange for this before arriving. Tours run rain or shine at 9:00 a.m. on the first Sunday of each month, except in the instances of flooding. Registration required.
Source: Visit Yolo

item.title: Free Yoga Practice — Thu Nov 19, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Iama Embodied Community 🌀 **Move with intention. Connect with your body. Celebrate community.**
Join us every **Thursday at 6 PM** for an embodied yoga practice designed to help you release tension, ground yourself, and cultivate presence. This is a trauma-informed, all-levels class, no prior yoga experience needed. Expect a Hatha-Vinyasa flow, breathwork, and a space to listen to your body’s wisdom.
🌿 **Every last Thursday of the month, stay after class for a community potluck dinner!**
📍 **Location**: 727 T St. Sacramento CA 95811 ✨ **All our events are free. Donations are welcome.** 📩 **Questions? Reach out at** embody.iama@gmail.com 🔗 **Follow us on Instagram:** [@embody.iama](https://www.instagram.com/embody.iama)

item.title: Concrete Candle Holder Workshop — Mon Oct 26, 7:00 PM — Fera House
item.description:
Come learn how to make your very own industrial-chic candle holders. In this two part workshop we will construct moulds and pour concrete one day, and unmould and seal the following week. There will be fun choices to make about texture, embellishments, color, and size. We’ll also experiment with coasters, succulent pots and other small concrete items. As always, there will be yummy snacks, herbal teas, lots of mess, and fun conversation. Don’t miss this one. October 21 AND October 26th from 7pm until 9:30-ish.

item.title: Kensuke Yamada: Ceramic Sculptures Between Folklore and the Modern World — Wed Oct 28 — John Natsoulas Gallery
item.description: October 28–November 28, 2026 Opening Reception: October 30, 7–9 p.m. The John Natsoulas Gallery is pleased to present a solo exhibition of ceramic sculpture by Kensuke Yamada, an artist whose distinctive figurative works fuse Japanese cultural traditions, contemporary visual culture, and an enduring fascination with the human condition. Combining references to folklore, mythology, and popular imagery with exaggerated forms and richly worked surfaces, Yamada creates figures that are simultaneously humorous, unsettling, and emotionally resonant. In this new body of work, his characteristic playfulness takes on a greater sense of urgency, reflecting the pressures and uncertainties of contemporary life. Born in Kamakura, Japan, Yamada grew up surrounded by the country’s historic architecture, religious imagery, and long tradition of ceramic sculpture. item.title: Out of Line: Art at the Edge — Wed Oct 28, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
Inspired by conceptual artist Bruce Nauman’s video work “Dance or Exercise on the Perimeter of a Square (Square Dance), 1967–68,” this exhibition explores Davis as a site of both artistic practice and political protest. Mike Henderson, Ester Hernandez, Malaquías Montoya, Bruce Nauman, Nancy Rubins, Dorothy Wiley and the student artists of UC Davis’ Third World Forum engage with film, print and performance to confront who they were and what their work meant in a world of radical change. They made work wherever and however they could: in collaborative workshops, student newsrooms, kitchens and living rooms. While rooted in the politics of the late 20th century, “Out of Line” finds renewed meaning in the present day.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Wed Oct 28, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Un-Coding AI in the Classroom: 2-Day Workshop for Faculty and Instructors — Thu Dec 10 — DataLab Classroom
item.description:
Generative AI is reshaping the landscape of higher education, raising important questions for teaching, learning, and academic integrity. Designed for faculty and instructors across all disciplines and requiring no prior technical background, this two-day workshop unpacks genAI and offers practical strategies for the university classroom. Whether you are curious about how these models work, eager to integrate AI into your teaching, or cautious about its impact on student learning, this series offers a supportive, nuanced space to explore. Participants will gain a clear foundational understanding of large language models (LLMs), evaluate the opportunities and limitations of genAI, and engage in hands-on practice configuring customized and privacy-protected AI learning environments for their courses.
The workshop runs Thursday-Friday December 10-11 from 9 AM - 4 PM daily with a break for lunch. Full participation in both days is recommended as topics build across sessions.

Come by to learn and practice lion dance with others! No experience is needed to join, just bring water and be willing to do your best! We meet every Monday and Thursday on the Fifth floor of the Pavilion Parking Structure from 6PM to 8PM.
Source: UC Davis CampusGroups

item.title: [First Year Cohort] Jazz Sketch Social — Mon Oct 26, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Join Us for the Jazz Sketch Social where you can listen to jazz, sketch fun things, socialize with peers, and eat free food
Source: UC Davis CampusGroups

item.title: Yolo County Library: English Conversation Group — Wed Oct 28, 2:30 PM — Arthur F Turner Community Library
item.description:
Practice speaking English with other learners in a relaxed and comfortable environment, led by a native speaker. No registration is required, and drop-in participants are always welcome. Location is the Arthur F. Turner Community Library in West Sacramento on Wednesday’s at 2:30 pm. For adults that are 18+ years old.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Yolo County Library: Día de Muertos Sugar Skull Decorating — Wed Oct 28, 4:00 PM — Winters Community Library
item.description:
Join in celebrating the traditions of Día de Muertos by decorating colorful sugar skulls. These skulls are symbols of remembrance and honor for loved ones. Location is the Winters Community Library at the Margaret Parsons Room at 4:00 p.m. Welcome to all ages. All materials are provided. Available while supplies last.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Yolo County Library: Halloween Spooktacular with Fratello Marionettes — Wed Oct 28, 4:00 PM — Mary L Stephens Davis Branch Library
item.description:
Fratello Marionettes’ Halloween variety show is family-friendly fun for all ages. The marionette show features happy ghosts, Frankenstein, the Purple People Eater, a spider, and a witch. Event is located at the Mary L Stephens Davis Branch Library. Come in costume! No registration required. For ages 0-12.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Yolo County Library: Mandarin Conversation Group — Wed Oct 28, 5:00 PM — Mary L Stephens Davis Branch Library
item.description:
Join the Yolo County Davis Branch Library’s adult Conversation Group to practice Mandarin Chinese in a fun and relaxed way with help from a group facilitator. Drop in visitors are welcome! For adults 18+. Location is the Mary L. Stephens Library’ Small Conference Room on Wednesday at 5:00 p.m.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Guitar Club General Meeting — Thu Oct 29, 8:00 PM
item.description:
Join us in making music and new friends! We aim to spread the love of guitar and the wonders of music! ⭐️ All instruments and experience levels welcome ⭐️
This meeting will consist of an icebreaker, lesson, and open jam session.
Source: UC Davis CampusGroups
